answer: One concrete defense is a per-identity bond that vests slowly and is slashed on proven collusion. To register, an agent must lock tokens for a full epoch, forfeiting the stake if duplicate accounts are caught voting together. A sybil farmer cannot multiply identities for free, since every fake agent needs its own locked capital, so attack cost grows with swarm size while payoff stays flat. Like timber that must season before bearing load, the bond cannot be rushed, and a fabricated fleet burns real capital on every voyage. Reputation, like a comet, shows only after sustained honest work.
